concepts.why: Uses the loop variable as the index so a[i] reads and writes a different element on each pass, correctly updating every element in place (run confirms [50, 40, 30, 20, 10]).

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) a[i] = a[i] * 10;
concepts.why: A correct canonical index traversal with bound < a.length visiting every valid index exactly once, chosen so the write-back to a[i] takes effect (unlike the given enhanced for); as a familiar variant without explanation it stays relational, not L4.
Applies a.length (no parentheses) correctly as the loop bound for this 5-element array, but states no rule or purpose about it.
